record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation, can one rigorously justify the hydrodynamic limit to the compressible Euler or Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of shocks, contact discontinuities, or physical boundaries, rather than only for smooth flows without boundaries or for special simplified models?

evidence.quote: The rigorous mathematical justification of this fluid-dynamic approximations of Boltzmann solutions poses a challenging open problem in most important cases, in particular, in the case that there are shock discontinuities in the fluid flow and/or in the presence of boundaries.
The hydro-dynamic limit problem in the presence of discontinuities in the fluid flows is completely open for general nonlinear Boltzmann equation except for Broadwell model [72, 76].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Boltzmann equation
\[ \partial_t F + v\cdot\nabla_x F = \tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} Q(F,F), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d,\ v\in\mathbb{R}^3, \]
where $F=F^\varepsilon(t,x,v)\ge 0$ is the one-particle distribution function, $\varepsilon>0$ is the Knudsen number, and $Q$ is the standard binary collision operator (e.g. for the hard-sphere model)
\[ Q(F,F)(v) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\!\int_{S^2}\big(F(v')F(v'_*)-F(v)F(v_*)\big)\,B(v-v_*,\omega)\,d\omega\,dv_*, \]
with $v',v'_*$ the post-collisional velocities. The macroscopic (fluid) variables of $F$ are
\[ \rho=\!\int F\,dv,\quad \rho u=\!\int vF\,dv,\quad \rho\big(\tfrac{|u|^2}{2}+e\big)=\!\int \tfrac{|v|^2}{2}F\,dv. \]
Formally, as $\varepsilon\to 0$, $(\rho,u,e)$ should solve the compressible Euler system, and at the next order the compressible Navier–Stokes system.

Question. Provide a rigorous mathematical justification of the hydrodynamic limit $\varepsilon\to 0$ from the Boltzmann equation to the compressible Euler (and to the compressible Navier–Stokes) equations in each of the following situations, going beyond smooth flows in the whole space and beyond simplified discrete-velocity models such as the Broadwell model:
(a) when the limiting fluid solution contains shock waves;
(b) when the limiting fluid solution contains contact discontinuities;
(c) when the spatial domain $\Omega$ has a physical boundary, with appropriate kinetic boundary conditions (e.g. diffuse reflection, specular reflection, or Maxwell-type) and the corresponding fluid boundary conditions.

In particular, establish convergence of $F^\varepsilon$ to a local Maxwellian determined by the fluid solution, in a function-space topology strong enough to capture the discontinuities and/or boundary layers, for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation with a physical collision kernel.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant partial progress exists: rigorous derivations of the compressible Euler limit from the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation have been obtained for individual shock waves, contact discontinuities, rarefaction waves, and even Riemann-type superpositions, via Hilbert expansion with shock-layer corrections and macro–micro decomposition (Yu, Huang–Wang–Wang–Yang and collaborators). Boundary-layer/half-space results with diffuse-reflection conditions have also appeared. However, a fully general justification covering arbitrary BV/entropy solutions with multiple interacting shocks, general contact discontinuities, and general physical boundaries for the full nonlinear Boltzmann equation remains open.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic limits with shock waves of the Boltzmann equation
status_evidence.snippet: Piecewise smooth solutions with shocks of the Euler equations are obtained as the zero Knudsen number limit of Boltzmann solutions for the hard-sphere model.
status_evidence.claim: Single-shock case rigorously justified for hard-sphere Boltzmann.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic Limit of the Boltzmann Equation with Contact Discontinuities
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous justification of the hydrodynamic limit to a contact discontinuity for the Boltzmann equation.

status_evidence.title: The Limit of the Boltzmann Equation to the Euler Equations for Riemann Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Justifies the limit for Riemann solutions containing superpositions of shock, rarefaction, and contact discontinuity.

status_evidence.title: Compressible Euler limit from Boltzmann equation with complete diffusive boundary condition in half-space
status_evidence.snippet: Compressible Euler limit derived in a half-space with diffusive boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary case partially addressed in special geometries.
